$comment: Which programme owns which repository, and which programmes may contribute to it. Hand-authored; validated by scripts/check-programme-claim.mjs. A repository owned by no programme is the defect Programme 12 was created to fix: 21 of 29 were unowned, and D001/D008/D148 were filed against code with no owner to fix them. Consumers are NOT stored here — the gate derives them live from package.json so they cannot go stale. See 40-PROGRAMME-12-PLATFORM-CORE.md § 1.

model.owner: Exactly one programme is accountable for a repository's health, standards and evolution.
model.contributors: Other programmes may write to declared path scopes inside it. This is not a weaker claim — it is the honest shape: Programme 3 builds the marketplace inside unierp-api, Programme 6 builds the admin console inside unierp-web. Pretending each programme has its own repository would have made the manifest wrong on the day it was written.
model.planned: A repository a programme will create but which does not exist yet. The gate does not require it on disk.

unierp-workspace.role: The programme plan, its tooling and its gates; integration and release surfaces.

unierp-web.role: The web client platform — the runtime the 903 route pages run on.

unierp-console.role: The provider control plane (plane 1): estate, reconciliation, release, cost.

unierp-developer.role: The developer portal: builders, sandbox surfaces, app lifecycle (plane 4).

unierp-corporate-website.role: unierp.com and its admin console (plane 0). Its own database, middleware and auth, deliberately separate.

unierp-design-system.role: The design system. Owned by Track B; every client programme extends it through its own design-system phase, which is why those are contributors rather than co-owners.

unierp-idp.role: Identity provider: authentication, federation, tokens, sessions. The most security-critical repository in the family.

unierp-data.role: Prisma schema, migrations and the data layer. Owns the model every service reads.

unierp-shared.role: Shared libraries used across every service.

unierp-framework.role: The application framework: request lifecycle, tenant context, middleware.

unierp-extensions.role: First-party extension implementations, built on the same public contract as third-party ones.

unierp-sandbox.role: The isolated runtime for untrusted extension and developer code.

unierp-contracts.role: The API contracts every client, SDK and type is generated from. The single source of truth for the API surface.

unierp-infra.role: Infrastructure definitions: environments, deployment, networking, secrets.

unierp-auth.role: Authorization primitives: permission evaluation, guards, record-level rules.

unierp-kernel.role: Core runtime primitives: module registration, lifecycle, composition.

unierp-service-kit.role: Service scaffolding — generates a service that is compliant by construction.

unierp-sdk.role: The published client SDK, layered over the generated client.

unierp-config.role: Shared configuration consumed by every repository.

unierp-platform.role: Aggregation repository. P12-201 decides whether it keeps that role or is retired with its content rehomed.

unierp-storybook.role: Published component documentation for the design system.

unierp-corporate-site-template.role: The starting template for tenant corporate sites, maintained against the current design system.

unierp-loop-a.role: Agent worktree. Hygiene rules apply; no committed evidence files or stray artefacts (D145).

unierp-loop-b.role: Agent worktree. Hygiene rules apply; no committed evidence files or stray artefacts (D145).

unierp-loop-c.role: Agent worktree. Hygiene rules apply; no committed evidence files or stray artefacts (D145).

unierp-studio.role: The tenant website builder, extracted from unierp-web/app/_sites into its own deployable.

unierp-desktop.role: Windows, macOS and Linux. Greenfield — the technology decision is P11-002.
